notes: The single-node profile's LiteLLM aliases — every one REQUIRED but cc-rerank (optional) and the speech pair with CC_ENABLE_SPEECH=0. Applied by setup.sh's llm phase through deploy/pi/litellm/register-models.py --policy — CREATE-ONLY: an absent alias is created as a skeleton with PLACEHOLDER where YOUR provider information goes (model id, api_base; the api key / credential you add in the UI), and an alias that exists is never written to. Setup then PAUSES (exit 3) on every fresh catalog so you fill them in at http://127.0.0.1:4000/ui before anything else is deployed; the re-run validates each alias with a real request and continues.

The catalog lives in LiteLLM's Postgres (store_model_in_db) and is managed through its UI/API — the config file is the fallback for what the API cannot set, never the default (operator decision, 2026-08-30). JSON so the pre-venv system python needs no PyYAML.

cc-default: what Central Command's agents address. The spine knows exactly one alias. Fill in model (openai/<id your server names>) and api_base (the URL the CONTAINER dials — never 127.0.0.1 for a server on this machine; use host.containers.internal).

graphiti-llm: a PLAIN openai/ alias, same as cc-default (2026-09-21) — the re-run REFUSES a value carrying the old openai/chat_completions/ bridge prefix. The app's in-process graphiti-core client (OpenAIGenericClient) POSTs /v1/chat/completions with a json_schema response_format; LiteLLM forwards that to llama.cpp unchanged. A chat_completions/ prefix forces LiteLLM's Responses->chat bridge instead, which sends 'chat_completions/<model>' upstream and 404s. Typically the same model id and api_base as cc-default.
cc-embedding: the embedder — commonly a different server than chat. Its DIMENSION is measured by setup and written into the Neo4j vector index — effectively permanent.

cc-rerank: OPTIONAL — graph search's reranker; the run never pauses for it (optional), and its skeleton is left for you. Declared in .env (CC_LLM_UPSTREAM_MODEL_CC_RERANK), setup REGISTERS AND PROBES it in order and keeps the row that answers: first as a dedicated reranker — cohere/<id> with the declared base ending /v1/rerank and mode rerank, the shape a llama.cpp --rerank server answers (the openai/ provider cannot answer LiteLLM's /rerank) — then as a chat model, openai/<id> on the declared base, asked one True/False question per candidate and scored from logprobs. An answer that names its provider (cohere/<id>, hosted_vllm/<id>, infinity/<id>) is registered verbatim as a dedicated reranker and probed only that way. A chat reranker MUST return logprobs and must NOT think first (a hybrid-thinking llama.cpp model needs chat_template_kwargs {"enable_thinking": false} on this row, exactly as graphiti-llm carries it; other gateways have their own switch — the probe is the judge). Entered in the UI instead, use whatever provider your reranker speaks; the skeleton's openai/ prefix is a starting point, not an invariant (judged_by_probe). With no dedicated reranker, the same model as graphiti-llm (thinking off) is the one-line choice: it costs up to 50 one-token calls per agent fact search on that model (twice the 25-fact limit the agent tools ask for). Left unmapped, search ranks by rank fusion alone. (gpt-4.1-nano, the alias graphiti-core's unused default reranker addressed, is no longer registered; an existing row is left alone.)

cc-tts / cc-stt: the cockpit's read-aloud and voice input (audio_speech / audio_transcription). With the bundled engine (CC_ENABLE_SPEECH=1) fill in openai/<CC_SPEECH_TTS_MODEL> and openai/<CC_SPEECH_STT_MODEL> with api_base http://<prefix>speech:8000/v1 and key `none` — setup prints the exact values. Either alias may point at an engine of your own instead (hosted Whisper-convention models for cc-stt is the expected case).
A key the server ignores can be a placeholder like `none`, but the field must be NON-EMPTY — LiteLLM needs a value to send.
